market.question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $200 by end of June?

assessment.reasoning: WTI front-month is currently trading around $94/bbl (late April 2026) after surging ~14-17% on the week driven by the Strait of Hormuz closure and the US-Iran conflict. The 52-week high reached $117.63. To hit $200, WTI would need a further ~112% rally from current levels in roughly 9 weeks — a move with virtually no precedent outside of the 1979 Iranian Revolution shock, and even then it took years. The EIA STEO forecasts Brent peaking at $115/bbl in Q2 2026 before easing, implying WTI well below $200. LiteFinance's bull-case analyst scenario mentions $150–$200 only as a tail-risk escalation scenario. The primary upside driver — Hormuz closure — is already largely priced in, and peace-talk hopes have already pulled prices back from intraday highs. Even the most bullish institutional forecast (LiteFinance ~$137 bull case for full-year 2026) falls far short of $200. The only realistic path to $200 WTI by June 30 would be a dramatic further military escalation causing near-total Gulf export collapse with no IEA/SPR response — a very low-probability tail event given ongoing diplomacy and the IEA's 400 mb emergency reserve release already announced.
data_sources: EIA STEO: Brent peaks at $115/bbl in Q2 2026, WTI averages $74/bbl for full-year 2026
Brent-WTI spread averaging $12/bbl in March 2026 (EIA STEO)
IEA: 400 mb emergency reserves released March 2026 to address supply disruptions
LiteFinance: bull-case analyst scenario of $150–$200 as conflict-escalation tail risk
Reuters poll (Feb 2026): WTI consensus average $60.38/bbl for full-year 2026
Barchart CLM26: June WTI closed ~$94-96 range late April 2026
assessment.key_uncertainty: Whether the US-Iran conflict escalates dramatically (e.g., full Hormuz blockade with major Gulf producer shut-ins and failed diplomacy), which is the only plausible path to $200; conversely, a peace deal would collapse prices well below current levels.
